title: Electro-Therapeutic Modalities for Pain Management (ETMPM) - Transcutaneous Electrical Nerve Stimulation (TENS) Procurement Program
description: Solicitation Notice: 36C79126R0011 � Electro-Therapeutic Modalities for Pain Management (ETMPM) � Transcutaneous Electrical Nerve Stimulation (TENS) Procurement Program Notice Type: Solicitation Issuance Notice Solicitation Number: 36C79126R0011 Posted Date: September 18, 2026 Response Due Date: October 19, 2026, 3:00 PM Central Daylight Time (CDT) NAICS Code: 334510 � Electromedical and Electrotherapeutic Apparatus Manufacturing. The Small Business size standard for NAICS Code 334510 is 1,250 employees. This NAICS code is appropriate as it encompasses the manufacturing of FDA?regulated electromedical therapeutic equipment including TENS, IFC, neuromodulation, and diathermy devices. PSC: 6515 � Medical and Surgical Instruments, Equipment, and Supplies Set-Aside: The Tiered Set-Aside Evaluation Approach used by the VA is not classified as a traditional Small Business set-aside, but rather as a competitive negotiated procurement, conducted via a tiered evaluation process aimed at prioritizing award to successive small business categories. This acquisition will be conducted using the VA Tiered Set?Aside Evaluation Approach pursuant to the authority of 38 U.S.C. 8127, including the statutory priority ordering prescribed in 38 U.S.C. �?8127(h) (a subsection of the Veterans First Contracting Program statute) and the procedures outlined in Veteran Affairs Acquisition Regulation (VAAR) 815.101?370 (Class Deviation). Under this approach, the Government will solicit offers from all tiers of Offerors simultaneously; however, proposal evaluations and award determination will occur sequentially in the prescribed order of priority. The tiers for this procurement are as follows: Tier-1 Service?Disabled Veteran?Owned Small Business (SDVOSB): SDVOSBs shall be evaluated first in accordance with VA�s statutory obligation to prioritize verified SDVOSBs when the VA Rule of Two is met. If no award can be made at Tier-1, then verified VOSB offers will be evaluated next in Tier-2, consistent with the Veterans First hierarchy. Tier-2 Veteran?Owned Small Business (VOSB): If no award can be made at Tier 2, the Government will evaluate offers from all other eligible small business concerns, (e.g., 8(a), HUBZone, and WOSB are considered before considering other small business concerns), in Tier 3 following the tiering procedures established in VAAR 815.101-3 and VAAR 815.101-370 (Class Deviation). Tier-3 Other Small Business Concerns: If no award can be made at Tier-3, the Government will evaluate offers from all Other-Than-Small-Business (OTSB) Concerns (Large Businesses)) in Tier 4 following the tiering procedures established in VAAR 815.101?3 and 815.101?370 (Class Deviation). Tier-4 Other?Than?Small Business (OTSB) Concerns (Large Businesses): If no award can be made under any small business Tier 1 through 3, the Government will evaluate offers from other?than?small businesses or large business concerns in Tier 4. This tiered evaluation methodology is authorized under 38 U.S.C. 8127 and implemented through the VA�s Class Deviation to VAAR 815.101?370, which permits the use of tiered set?aside procedures to minimize procurement delays in situations where market research indicates that award at the SDVOSB or VOSB tiers is uncertain. Contracting Office: Department of Veterans Affairs, Enterprise Procurement Office, Acquisition Service Four Delta Team, 555 Corporate Circle, Golden, CO 80401-5621. Introduction: The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) is pleased to announce the release of Solicitation Number 36C79126R0011, the official Request for Proposals (RFP) for the Electro-Therapeutic Modalities for Pain Management (ETMPM) � Transcutaneous Electrical Nerve Stimulation (TENS) Procurement Program. The objective of this national procurement program is to establish multiple single-awards of Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP), Indefinite Delivery/Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) Base contracts and resultant FFP/IDIQ Delivery Order contracts to be awarded on a per-Contract Line Item Number (CLIN) and per-Sub-Line Item Number (SLIN) basis for the procurement of FDA-cleared electro-therapeutic devices and accessories supporting non-opioid pain management for Veterans across all VA Medical Centers and Community-Based Outpatient Clinics. This solicitation recompetition of the expiring legacy TENS contract and expands the legacy TENS procurement program to include Interferential Current Therapy (IFC) devices, Short-Wave Diathermy (SWD) devices (thermal and non-thermal), and portable Neuromodulation systems - for the treatment of headache disorders to be inclusive all unique parent CLIN devices and the device accessories has enumerated at the discrete subordinate SLINs. The device accessories categorized as SLINs include but are not limited to electrodes, lead wires, power chargers, garment-based applicators, and associated other consumables. Each product of the ETMPM-TENS requirement is mapped to unique parent CLIN and a discrete subordinate SLINs with universal Minimum Technical Requirements (MTRs) applicable to all CLINs/SLINs and individual CLIN/SLIN-specific MTRs. Anticipated Award: The results of competition ultimately determine when and if award(s) can be made, but the VA intends to finalize award decisions on or before but no later than January 19, 2027, the expiration date of the legacy TENS contract. The VA reserves the right not to make an award or to make award on some CLINs/SLINs but not all the CLINs/SLINs enumerated in the solicitation. title: Notice of Intent to Sole Source Association for Computing Machinery e-Journals
description: The US Army Corps of Engineers, Engineer Research and Development Center (ERDC), intends to issue an award to Association for Computing Machinery, 1601 Broadway, 10th Floor, New York, NY 10019-7434, a sole source basis utilizing Simplified Acquisition Procedures as outlined in FAR Part 12. The requirement is for multiple physical site licenses for the following journals: Association for Computing Machinery (ACM) Journal publications. The license is propriety to ACM; Association for Computing Machinery is the sole source provider of the complete ACM Digital Library and ACM Open Licenses for the institutional library market. ACM holds exclusive worldwide distribution rights for the ACM Digital Library and ACM Open. The NAICS code for this requirement is 513120 with a size standard of 1000 employees. This notice is not a request for competitive quotes or proposals. A solicitation will not be issued; however, all responsible sources may submit a capability statement, proposal, or quotation, which shall be considered by the agency. The information submitted must be provided in sufficient detail to demonstrate the vendor s ability to fulfill this requirement. The contractor must also provide a description of their past experience in fulfilling requirements which are the same or similar to this requirement and references for each. Information received will be considered solely for the purpose of determining whether to conduct competitive procurement. A determination by the Government not to compete this requirement on a full and open competition basis, based upon responses to this notice, is solely within the discretion of the government. Oral communications are not acceptable in response to this notice. Interested parties may submit any information for consideration by the Government to TriNeciya.C.Winford@usace.army.mil. The notice number shall be included in the subject line of e-mail submissions. Responses should be received by date specified above.

PSC: 6515 � Medical and Surgical Instruments, Equipment, and Supplies Set-Aside: The Tiered Set-Aside Evaluation Approach used by the VA is not classified as a traditional Small Business set-aside, but rather as a competitive negotiated procurement, conducted via a tiered evaluation process aimed at prioritizing award to successive small business categories. This acquisition will be conducted using the VA Tiered Set?Aside Evaluation Approach pursuant to the authority of 38 U.S.C. 8127, including the statutory priority ordering prescribed in 38 U.S.C. �?8127(h) (a subsection of the Veterans First Contracting Program statute) and the procedures outlined in Veteran Affairs Acquisition Regulation (VAAR) 815.101?370 (Class Deviation). Under this approach, the Government will solicit offers from all tiers of Offerors simultaneously; however, proposal evaluations and award determination will occur sequentially in the prescribed order of priority. Tier-2 Veteran?Owned Small Business (VOSB): If no award can be made at Tier 2, the Government will evaluate offers from all other eligible small business concerns, (e.g., 8(a), HUBZone, and WOSB are considered before considering other small business concerns), in Tier 3 following the tiering procedures established in VAAR 815.101-3 and VAAR 815.101-370 (Class Deviation). title: Maintenance Dredging of the Isle au Haut Thoroughfare near Isle au Haut, Maine
description: The Isle au Haut Thoroughfare Federal Navigation Project, located between Isle au Haut, Maine and Kimball Island, Maine on the outskirts of Penobscot Bay, about six miles southeast of Stonington and 25 miles east of Rockland. The Federal Navigation Project consists of a -6-foot Mean Lower Low Water (MLLW) deep by 75-foot wide extending 1,200-foot in length through the shoal in the thoroughfare.The proposed work consists of mechanically dredging approximately 3,355 cubic yards (cy) (1,183 cy required, plus 2,172 cy overdepth) of shoaled material consisting of highly compacted coarse sand and gravel, with areas of cobbles and isolated small boulders from the channel. Due to the material type, a mechanical dredge with the ability to dig highly compacted coarse sand and gravel will be required. The proposed action is to dredge to the authorized depth of -6-foot MLLW plus an additional 1-foot of required advance maintenance with an additional allowable 1-foot of overdepth (e.g. -7-foot MLLW required + 1-foot allowable OD). One-time, advanced maintenance is approved for the entirety of the 1200-foot long authorized channel. The dredged material will be placed at the Flake Island Disposal Site (FIDS) which is approximately 1 nautical mile northwest of the FNP. Placement of the dredged material (sand, gravel and cobble) at Flake Island Disposal Site will benefit both juvenile lobster habitat and juvenile cod by increasing the areas habitat complexity.The anticipated allowable dredging window is between September 15 and April 1 to avoid impacts to spawning shellfish, benthic resources, Essential Fish Habitat (EFH) of federally managed species, threatened and endangered species and interactions with mobile fishing gear.

REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) BUILDING 215 ADVANCED MEASUREMENT LABORATORY (AML) CLEANROOM REPAIR AND HEPA FILTER REPLACEMENT Solicitation/Reference No.: 1333ND26RNB190014 1. PURPOSE OF THIS REQUEST FOR INFORMATION The National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) is conducting market research pursuant to Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Part 10 and FAR 15.201 to obtain industry feedback concerning the scope, schedule, phasing, cleanroom outage requirements, technical and performance risks, and estimated construction cost associated with the Building 215 Advanced Measurement Laboratory (AML) Cleanroom Repair and HEPA Filter Replacement project. NIST previously solicited this requirement under Solicitation No. 1333ND26RNB190014. NIST did not receive an acceptable offer under that solicitation. NIST is therefore reassessing the requirement and acquisition approach before determining whether and how to resolicit the project. NIST is particularly interested in identifying aspects of the requirement that may materially affect industry participation, constructability, schedule feasibility, pricing, risk, or the ability of contractors to submit competitive proposals. Industry is encouraged to provide candid feedback and to identify recommended changes that could improve constructability, competition, schedule feasibility, cost certainty, and overall project execution while continuing to meet NIST�s mission and cleanroom operational requirements. 2. RFI / MARKET RESEARCH NOTICE THIS RFI IS ISSUED SOLELY FOR INFORMATION AND ACQUISITION PLANNING PURPOSES. IT DOES NOT CONSTITUTE A REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL (RFP), INVITATION FOR BID (IFB), REQUEST FOR QUOTATION (RFQ), OR OTHER SOLICITATION. The Government does not intend to award a contract based on responses to this RFI. Responses will be treated as information only and shall not be construed as offers or proposals that can be accepted by the Government to form a binding contract. The Government will not reimburse respondents for costs incurred in preparing or submitting information in response to this RFI or for participating in any follow-up discussions. This RFI does not obligate the Government to issue a solicitation or award a contract, nor does it restrict the Government�s ultimate acquisition approach. Respondents are advised that information submitted in response to this RFI may be used by NIST in developing or revising the acquisition strategy, statement of work, specifications, schedule, phasing requirements, outage requirements, Government cost estimate, and future solicitation. Respondents should clearly identify and mark any proprietary, confidential, or commercially sensitive information contained in their responses. Respondents should avoid including proprietary information unless necessary to provide a meaningful response. 3. PROJECT BACKGROUND The project involves repair and modernization work within the Building 215 Advanced Measurement Laboratory cleanroom located at the NIST Gaithersburg Campus. The AML cleanroom encompasses approximately 1,800 square meters and includes approximately 750 square meters of Class 100 cleanroom space. The facility supports sensitive NIST research activities and contains specialized and, in some instances, irreplaceable scientific equipment. The project generally includes, but is not limited to: Replacement of approximately 1,200 terminal supply HEPA filters; Repair and/or modification of HEPA filter connections; Testing, balancing, certification, and recertification of affected HEPA filters and cleanroom spaces; Replacement of approximately 70 variable air volume (VAV) terminal units; Replacement of approximately 54 airflow monitoring devices; Installation of approximately 32 exhaust air control valves; Modification and repair of associated ductwork; Rebalancing of associated air-handling and exhaust systems; Verification and repair, as required, of existing capped ductwork; Controls-related work; Cleaning, testing, balancing, commissioning, and cleanroom certification associated with each affected area; and Protection of existing cleanroom spaces, research operations, and sensitive scientific equipment throughout construction. Detailed project drawings, specifications, and/or relevant portions of the previously issued solicitation may be attached to this RFI or otherwise made available through SAM.gov for purposes of industry review. 4. CURRENT PHASING AND OUTAGE CONCEPT NIST�s previous acquisition strategy was developed to minimize disruption to ongoing research operations by performing the work through phased cleanroom outages rather than shutting down the entire cleanroom for the duration of construction. The previous requirement contemplated 19 construction phases consisting of 18 Critical Cleanroom Outage Phases and one Non-Critical Phase. For each Critical Cleanroom Outage Phase, the contemplated outage period was approximately nine calendar days, generally structured as follows: Outage/construction activities begin at approximately 7:00 p.m. on Friday; Work proceeds continuously, including 24-hour-per-day/seven-day-per-week operations, as necessary; Construction, startup, testing, balancing, cleaning, commissioning, and applicable cleanroom certification are completed during the outage period; and The affected cleanroom area is required to achieve Ready for Re-Occupancy by approximately 7:00 a.m. on the second following Monday. Ready for Re-Occupancy generally means that required construction, startup, testing, balancing, cleaning, commissioning, and applicable cleanroom certification have been completed; the affected area is operationally capable of supporting its intended use without material restriction; and no deficiencies remain that materially impair safe occupancy or cleanroom operations. title: SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE FOR PROJECT LABOR AGGREEMENTS (PLAs) TO COASTAL STORM RISK MANAGEMENT (CSRM) FOR CAPE MAY TO LOWER TOWNSHIP, NEW JERSEY, BRIGANTINE INLET TO GREAT EGG HARBOR INLET (ABSECON ISLAND), NEW JERSEY, AND BARNEGAT INLET TO LITTLE EGG, INLET
description: The US Army Corps of Engineers, Enterprise Dredge Delivery Center (EDDC), is soliciting comments from the construction community addressing the potential use of Project Labor Agreements (PLA) for a large-scale construction project (exceeding $35 million) within the Cape May To Lower Township, New Jersey, Brigantine Inlet To Great Egg Harbor Inlet (Absecon Island), New Jersey, And Barnegat Inlet To Little Egg, Inlet (Long Beach Island), New Jersey area. This procurement is for Coastal Storm Risk Management (CSRM). Cape May to Lower Township, NJ (Navigation Mitigation � Beachfill): Work for the beachfill placement dredging will require a hopper and pipeline/mechanical dredge(s). The dredge(s) must have the capability to dredge material up to a depth of -40 ft NAVD88 and to transport the dredged sand to the designated areas approximately 2.6 miles away. The project for navigation mitigation (beach nourishment) is located on the Atlantic coast of New Jersey, extending from the Cape May Inlet southwest jetty to the 3rd Ave terminal groin in Cape May City. It includes the communities of the City of Cape May and Lower Township, and the US Coast Guard Training Center. The contract work will consist of a base bid to conduct pre-placement condition surveys and pump/place 600,000 cubic yards of sand from two borrow areas approximately 2.6 miles south of the Cape May Inlet jetties onto the beach at 2 locations: Area 1 (540,000 cu yds), the US Coast Guard Training Center and Area 2 (60,000 cu yds), Wilmington Ave. Options to place additional sand (100,000 cu yds) from the same borrow areas to achieve the full project design template at these same two beach locations will also be included. Sand must come from the offshore borrow areas. Trucking-in sand will not be permitted under this contract. All work under the contract must be completed no later than 1 March 2028. Brigantine Inlet to Great Egg Harbor Inlet (Absecon Island), NJ (CSRM � Beachfill): Contract work consists of a base bid to place approximately 1,500,000 cubic yards of beachfill, along the Atlantic Ocean coastline of Absecon Island, Atlantic County, New Jersey. The project area encompasses the municipalities of Atlantic City, Ventnor, Margate, and Longport. The contract work may also consist of separate options to place additional amounts of beachfill per option, if awarded, in locations within and outside of the Base bid areas. The project work for the Base Bid and Options, if awarded, also may include, in addition to beachfill: the construction or repair of pedestrian, vehicle, and ADA compliant dune crossovers; planting dune grass; installing sand fencing; the repair or extension of existing storm water outfalls and drainage structures; and the relocation or removal of various existing structures or fill to accommodate the beachfill and dunes. The beachfill material for this contract must come from the authorized borrow areas, which are shown on the contract drawings, located within and adjacent to the Absecon Inlet in the Atlantic Ocean, and a separate designated area located approximately 2 � 3 miles offshore of Absecon Island in the Atlantic Ocean. Barnegat Inlet to Little Egg, Inlet (Long Beach Island), NJ (CSRM � Beachfill): Contract work consists of a base bid to place approximately 2,000,000 cubic yards of beachfill to repair the dune and berm system along the Atlantic Ocean coastline of Long Beach Island, Ocean County, New Jersey. The project area encompasses the municipalities of Long Beach Township, Borough of Harvey Cedars, Borough of Surf City, Borough of Ship Bottom, and Borough of Beach Haven. The contract work may also consist of separate options to place additional amounts of beachfill per option, if awarded, in locations within and outside of the Base bid areas. The project work for the Base Bid and Options, if awarded, also may include, in addition to beachfill: the construction or repair of pedestrian, vehicle, and ADA compatible dune crossovers; planting dune grass; providing sand fencing; and the relocation or removal of various existing structures to accommodate the beachfill, dunes and other project features. The beachfill material for this contract must come from the authorized borrow areas located approximately 2-3 miles offshore of Long Beach Island in the Atlantic Ocean, and/or the Little Egg Inlet as designated on the contract drawings. The solicitation is expected to be available in FY2027. A PLA is defined as a pre-hire collective bargaining agreement with one or more labor organizations that establishes the terms and conditions of employment for a specific construction project and is an agreement described in 29 U.S.C 158(f). Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Policy: (a) Project Labor Agreement (PLA) is a tool that agencies may use to promote economy and efficiency in Federal procurement. Pursuant to Executive Order 14063, agencies are encouraged to consider requiring the use of project labor agreements in connection with large-scale construction projects. (b) An agency may, if appropriate, require that every contractor and subcontractor engaged in construction on the project agree, for that project, to negotiate or become a party to a project labor agreement with one or more labor organizations if the agency decides that the use of project labor agreements will (1) Advance the Federal Government's interest in achieving economy and efficiency in Federal procurement, producing labor-management stability, and ensuring compliance with laws and regulations governing safety and health, equal employment opportunity, labor and employment standards, and other matters; and (2) Be consistent with law. Reference: Provision: 52.222-33 Notice of Requirement for Project Labor Agreement and Clause 52.222-34 Project Labor Agreement. (i) Requested are responses to the following: 1) Do you have knowledge that a PLA has been used in the local area on projects of this kind? If so, please provide supporting documentation. 2) Are you aware of skilled labor shortages in the area for those crafts that will be needed to complete the referenced project? If so, please elaborate and provide supporting documentation where possible. 3) Are you aware of time sensitive issues/scheduling requirements that would affect the rate at which the referenced project should be completed? If so, please elaborate and provide supporting documentation where possible. 4) Identify specific reasons why or how you believe a PLA would advance the Federal Government�s interest in achieving economy and efficiency in Federal procurement. 5) Identify specific reasons why you do not believe a PLA would advance the Federal Government�s interest in achieving economy and efficiency in Federal procurement. 6) Identify any additional information you believe the Government should take into consideration regarding the use of a PLA on the referenced project. 7) Does your company intend to bid/propose on this project if a PLA requirement is included in the solicitation? Does your company intend to bid/propose on this project if a PLA requirement is not included in the solicitation? 8) What are the likely cost impacts, if any, to your bid/proposal price if a PLA requirement is included in the solicitation? Please provide as much detail as possible regarding any anticipated cost impacts (positive or negative) of the inclusion of a PLA requirement, including any information you can provide about the magnitude of the anticipated impact. (ii) The information gathered in this exercise should include the following information on projects completed in the last 2-5 years (or other timeframe, as appropriate): 1) Project Name and Location: 2) Detailed Project Description: 3) Initial Cost Estimate vs. Actual Final Cost: 4) Was the project completed on time? 5) Number of craft trades present on the project: 6) Was a PLA used? 7) Were there any challenges experienced during the project? Responses shall be submitted via email to Terri Adams

title: SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE FOR PROJECT LABOR AGGREEMENTS (PLAs) TO COASTAL STORM RISK MANAGEMENT (CSRM) FOR CAPE MAY TO LOWER TOWNSHIP, NEW JERSEY, BRIGANTINE INLET TO GREAT EGG HARBOR INLET (ABSECON ISLAND), NEW JERSEY, AND BARNEGAT INLET TO LITTLE EGG, INLET
description: The US Army Corps of Engineers, Enterprise Dredge Delivery Center (EDDC), is soliciting comments from the construction community addressing the potential use of Project Labor Agreements (PLA) for a large-scale construction project (exceeding $35 million) within the Cape May To Lower Township, New Jersey, Brigantine Inlet To Great Egg Harbor Inlet (Absecon Island), New Jersey, And Barnegat Inlet To Little Egg, Inlet (Long Beach Island), New Jersey area. This procurement is for Coastal Storm Risk Management (CSRM). Cape May to Lower Township, NJ (Navigation Mitigation � Beachfill): Work for the beachfill placement dredging will require a hopper and pipeline/mechanical dredge(s). The dredge(s) must have the capability to dredge material up to a depth of -40 ft NAVD88 and to transport the dredged sand to the designated areas approximately 2.6 miles away. The project for navigation mitigation (beach nourishment) is located on the Atlantic coast of New Jersey, extending from the Cape May Inlet southwest jetty to the 3rd Ave terminal groin in Cape May City. It includes the communities of the City of Cape May and Lower Township, and the US Coast Guard Training Center. The contract work will consist of a base bid to conduct pre-placement condition surveys and pump/place 600,000 cubic yards of sand from two borrow areas approximately 2.6 miles south of the Cape May Inlet jetties onto the beach at 2 locations: Area 1 (540,000 cu yds), the US Coast Guard Training Center and Area 2 (60,000 cu yds), Wilmington Ave. Options to place additional sand (100,000 cu yds) from the same borrow areas to achieve the full project design template at these same two beach locations will also be included. Sand must come from the offshore borrow areas. Trucking-in sand will not be permitted under this contract. All work under the contract must be completed no later than 1 March 2028. Brigantine Inlet to Great Egg Harbor Inlet (Absecon Island), NJ (CSRM � Beachfill): Contract work consists of a base bid to place approximately 1,500,000 cubic yards of beachfill, along the Atlantic Ocean coastline of Absecon Island, Atlantic County, New Jersey. The project area encompasses the municipalities of Atlantic City, Ventnor, Margate, and Longport. The contract work may also consist of separate options to place additional amounts of beachfill per option, if awarded, in locations within and outside of the Base bid areas. The project work for the Base Bid and Options, if awarded, also may include, in addition to beachfill: the construction or repair of pedestrian, vehicle, and ADA compliant dune crossovers; planting dune grass; installing sand fencing; the repair or extension of existing storm water outfalls and drainage structures; and the relocation or removal of various existing structures or fill to accommodate the beachfill and dunes. The beachfill material for this contract must come from the authorized borrow areas, which are shown on the contract drawings, located within and adjacent to the Absecon Inlet in the Atlantic Ocean, and a separate designated area located approximately 2 � 3 miles offshore of Absecon Island in the Atlantic Ocean. Barnegat Inlet to Little Egg, Inlet (Long Beach Island), NJ (CSRM � Beachfill): Contract work consists of a base bid to place approximately 2,000,000 cubic yards of beachfill to repair the dune and berm system along the Atlantic Ocean coastline of Long Beach Island, Ocean County, New Jersey. The project area encompasses the municipalities of Long Beach Township, Borough of Harvey Cedars, Borough of Surf City, Borough of Ship Bottom, and Borough of Beach Haven. The contract work may also consist of separate options to place additional amounts of beachfill per option, if awarded, in locations within and outside of the Base bid areas. The project work for the Base Bid and Options, if awarded, also may include, in addition to beachfill: the construction or repair of pedestrian, vehicle, and ADA compatible dune crossovers; planting dune grass; providing sand fencing; and the relocation or removal of various existing structures to accommodate the beachfill, dunes and other project features. The beachfill material for this contract must come from the authorized borrow areas located approximately 2-3 miles offshore of Long Beach Island in the Atlantic Ocean, and/or the Little Egg Inlet as designated on the contract drawings. The solicitation is expected to be available in FY2027. A PLA is defined as a pre-hire collective bargaining agreement with one or more labor organizations that establishes the terms and conditions of employment for a specific construction project and is an agreement described in 29 U.S.C 158(f). Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Policy: (a) Project Labor Agreement (PLA) is a tool that agencies may use to promote economy and efficiency in Federal procurement. Pursuant to Executive Order 14063, agencies are encouraged to consider requiring the use of project labor agreements in connection with large-scale construction projects. (b) An agency may, if appropriate, require that every contractor and subcontractor engaged in construction on the project agree, for that project, to negotiate or become a party to a project labor agreement with one or more labor organizations if the agency decides that the use of project labor agreements will (1) Advance the Federal Government's interest in achieving economy and efficiency in Federal procurement, producing labor-management stability, and ensuring compliance with laws and regulations governing safety and health, equal employment opportunity, labor and employment standards, and other matters; and (2) Be consistent with law. Reference: Provision: 52.222-33 Notice of Requirement for Project Labor Agreement and Clause 52.222-34 Project Labor Agreement. (i) Requested are responses to the following: 1) Do you have knowledge that a PLA has been used in the local area on projects of this kind? If so, please provide supporting documentation. 2) Are you aware of skilled labor shortages in the area for those crafts that will be needed to complete the referenced project? If so, please elaborate and provide supporting documentation where possible. 3) Are you aware of time sensitive issues/scheduling requirements that would affect the rate at which the referenced project should be completed? If so, please elaborate and provide supporting documentation where possible. 4) Identify specific reasons why or how you believe a PLA would advance the Federal Government�s interest in achieving economy and efficiency in Federal procurement. 5) Identify specific reasons why you do not believe a PLA would advance the Federal Government�s interest in achieving economy and efficiency in Federal procurement. 6) Identify any additional information you believe the Government should take into consideration regarding the use of a PLA on the referenced project. 7) Does your company intend to bid/propose on this project if a PLA requirement is included in the solicitation? Does your company intend to bid/propose on this project if a PLA requirement is not included in the solicitation? 8) What are the likely cost impacts, if any, to your bid/proposal price if a PLA requirement is included in the solicitation? Please provide as much detail as possible regarding any anticipated cost impacts (positive or negative) of the inclusion of a PLA requirement, including any information you can provide about the magnitude of the anticipated impact. (ii) The information gathered in this exercise should include the following information on projects completed in the last 2-5 years (or other timeframe, as appropriate): 1) Project Name and Location: 2) Detailed Project Description: 3) Initial Cost Estimate vs. Actual Final Cost: 4) Was the project completed on time? 5) Number of craft trades present on the project: 6) Was a PLA used? 7) Were there any challenges experienced during the project? Responses shall be submitted via email to Terri Adams

description: 22 October 2026- The purpose of amendment 0003 is to extend the proposal due date from 26 October 2026 at 12:00 PM PT to 2 November 2026 at 12:00 PM PT. ____________________ 14 October 2026-The purpose of amendment 0002 is to extend the RFC due date from 8 October 2026 at 12:00 PM PT to 15 October 2026 at 12:00 PM PT and the proposal due date from 19 October 2026 at 12:00 PM PT to 26 October 2026 at 12:00 PM PT. See section L. ____________________ The Regional Maintenance Center at Puget Sound Naval Shipyard and Intermediate Maintenance Facility (PSNS and IMF) intends to award a stand-alone Firm-Fixed-Price contract to accomplish maintenance, repair, and preservation of YRBM-50. The YRBM-50 characteristics are Length: 153FT, Width: 43FT, Age: 82 Years, Hull Type: Steel, Draft: 6FT, Full Displacement: 900 L Tons and Light Load: 427 L Tons. The Contractors facility must possess the capability of YRBM-50 with the dimensions as stated above. To facilitate proper government oversight, the facility shall be located in the Puget Sound, WA region. For this procurement, the Puget Sound, WA region is defined as the West Coast of the continental US, starting from Olympia, WA and extending northward to Bellingham, WA. Scope Overview: Coordinate with the Contracting Officer, via the SUPERVISOR to deliver the vessel to the Contractors facility. To facilitate proper government oversight, the facility where the work will be performed shall be located in the Puget Sound, WA region. For this procurement, the Puget Sound, WA region is defined as the west of the continental US, starting from Olympia, WA and extending northward to Bellingham, WA. Upon docking vessel, wash, and clean vessel. Accomplish required inspections and fender repairs. Remove existing and install new zinc anodes. Hull, freeboard and exterior decks require ultrasonic measurement of plating thickness and repair of areas below minimum thickness as needed. Accomplish blast and paint preservation of hull, freeboard, exterior decks and superstructure. Vessel requires inspection for damage and deterioration (hull, exterior decks, and tanks/voids plating and framing). Apply new non-skid system to exterior decks. Open, clean, ventilate, inspect, test, and maintain dry each tank/void. Accomplish partial preservation of QTY (24 EA) ballast tanks/voids. Accomplish access cover and watertight hatch and door repairs. Disinfect and certify potable water system. Pump and clean the interior surfaces of the CHT tank. Accomplish main deck repairs, hawse hole bulls eye and bolster repairs, and hull fendering system modifications. Accomplish the following modifications: hot water heater installation, awning replacement, A/C plant replacement and backup systems, switchboard upgrades, 1MC replacement and phone system upgrades, and CCTV upgrades. Undock the vessel. Verify vessel drawings and provide redline drawings to reflect actual conditions of the vessel. Conduct dock trials. Coordinate with the SUPERVISOR to support and accomplish all contract requirements prior to the availability end date. Arrange and coordinate the delivery of the vessel back to the Government with the Contracting Officer via the SUPERVISOR. Specific details of all work items and tasks required by the Statement of Work described in this Scope Overview are included in Section 3.0 of the Statement of Work. The vessel availability is scheduled to be 31 March 2027 through 31 March 2028. description: The US Army Corps of Engineers, Enterprise Dredge Delivery Center (EDDC), is soliciting comments from the construction community addressing the potential use of Project Labor Agreements (PLA) for a large-scale construction project (exceeding $35 million) within the Bethany Beach and South Bethany Beach, DE (CSRM - Beachfill), Fenwick Island, DE (CSRM � Beachfill), and Rehoboth Beach & Dewey Beach, DE (CSRM � Beachfill): areas. This procurement is for Coastal Storm Risk Management (CSRM). Bethany Beach and South Bethany Beach, DE (CSRM - Beachfill): The work for the Bethany Beach and South Bethany Beach, CRSM projects will include periodic renourishment of the beach berm and dune to the original design template. It is estimated that approximately 532,000 cubic yards of sand would be required to restore Bethany Beach and South Bethany Beach to the original design template and approximately 165,000 CY of optional sand could be provided for advanced nourishment for the project. The base bid work would also include repair/replacement of dune grass, fencing and crossovers. Borrow Area E will be the source used for sand to restore this beach area and will require the use of a hopper or hydraulic cutterhead since Borrow Area E is located approximately two to three miles offshore of the Town of South Bethany. Fenwick Island, DE (CSRM � Beachfill): The work for the Fenwick Island, CRSM project will include periodic renourishment of the beach berm and dune to the original design template. It is estimated that approximately 207,000 cubic yards of sand would be required to restore Fenwick Island to the original design template and approximately 60,000 CY of optional sand could be provided for advanced nourishment for the project. The base bid work would also include repair/replacement of dune grass, fencing and crossovers. The Fenwick Island borrow area will be the source used for sand to restore this beach area and will require the use of a hopper or hydraulic cutterhead since the Fenwick Borrow Area is located approximately one to three miles offshore of the Town of Fenwick Island. Rehoboth Beach & Dewey Beach, DE (CSRM � Beachfill): The work for the Rehoboth Beach to Dewey Beach, CRSM projects will include periodic renourishment of the beach berm and dune to the original design template. It is estimated that approximately 390,000 cubic yards of sand would be required to restore Rehoboth Beach and Dewey Beach to the design template and approximately 120,000 CY of optional sand could be provided for advanced nourishment for the project. The base bid work would also include repair/replacement of dune grass, fencing and crossovers. title: F108--657A4-21-800 - VPIH Services for Remove and Replace End of Life Heating, Ventilation and Air Conditioning Construction
description: The purpose of this modification (#1) is to answer questions: Question 1: Typically, VPIH means Veterans Professional Industrial Hygienist which generally falls under NAICS code 541620 (Environmental Consulting). Could you please clarify what your definition of VPIH is and why you chose 562910 (Remediation Services). Answer: The NAICS code is changed to 541620 (Environmental Consulting). Question 2: The Scope of Work appeared rather vague in what the duties of the VPIH would be "VPIH firm to provide VPIH Services for construction project 657A4-21-800" Based on my experience as VPIH, that means overseeing asbestos abatement activities, visual inspections, air clearance sampling, etc. Could you please provide more details on what you envision the VPIH duties entailing. Answer: Here are more details about the project. Full details will be provided in the request for proposal to the top firm. - The VA Professional Industrial Hygienist (VPIH) shall provide all labor, materials, equipment and supervision necessary to review abatement personnel s documentation compliance monitoring, Phase Contrast Microscopy (PCM) air monitoring & analysis, inspections, clearance testing, and removal activities for the duration of the abatement as required by the project plans and specifications. - Asbestos/Lead abatement project oversight work will be performed in separate locations in Building 1 based on design documents. - The VPIH shall provide a final report for each location, at the end of the Asbestos Containment Material (ACM) abatement, which includes a summary of pre-abatement and post-abatement activities. - All routine air sample results shall be delivered to the Contracting Officer s Representative (COR) within 24 hours of collection. All clearance samples shall be delivered to the COR within 24 hours from the collection. Question 3: Generally Consulting services, if this is for a VPIH, do not require an SF 330 submittal. Could you please explain why this is apparently requiring an SF 330 submittal directed at A/E firms. Answer: This project is being solicited as an A/E project. Therefore, SF 330s are required. -----------------------END------------------------

It is estimated that approximately 532,000 cubic yards of sand would be required to restore Bethany Beach and South Bethany Beach to the original design template and approximately 165,000 CY of optional sand could be provided for advanced nourishment for the project. The base bid work would also include repair/replacement of dune grass, fencing and crossovers. The Fenwick Island borrow area will be the source used for sand to restore this beach area and will require the use of a hopper or hydraulic cutterhead since the Fenwick Borrow Area is located approximately one to three miles offshore of the Town of Fenwick Island. The anticipated acquisition will be a competitive, firm-fixed-price (FFP), design-bid-build (DBB), definitive contract. description: 22 October 2026- The purpose of this amendment is to extend the proposal due date from 26 October 2026 at 12:00 PM PT to 2 November 2026 at 12:00 PM PT.____________________ 14 October 2026-The purpose of this amendment is to extend the RFC due date from 8 October 2026 at 12:00 PM PT to 15 October 2026 at 12:00 PM PT and the proposal due date from 19 October 2026 at 12:00 PM PT to 26 October 2026 at 12:00 PM PT. See section L. ____________________The Regional Maintenance Center at Puget Sound Naval Shipyard and Intermediate Maintenance Facility (PSNS and IMF) intends to award a stand-alone Firm-Fixed-Price contract to accomplish maintenance, repair, and preservation of YRBM-50. The YRBM-50 characteristics are Length: 153FT, Width: 43FT, Age: 82 Years, Hull Type: Steel, Draft: 6FT, Full Displacement: 900 L Tons and Light Load: 427 L Tons. The Contractors facility must possess the capability of YRBM-50 with the dimensions as stated above. To facilitate proper government oversight, the facility shall be located in the Puget Sound, WA region. For this procurement, the Puget Sound, WA region is defined as the West Coast of the continental US, starting from Olympia, WA and extending northward to Bellingham, WA. Scope Overview: Coordinate with the Contracting Officer, via the SUPERVISOR to deliver the vessel to the Contractors facility. To facilitate proper government oversight, the facility where the work will be performed shall be located in the Puget Sound, WA region. For this procurement, the Puget Sound, WA region is defined as the west of the continental US, starting from Olympia, WA and extending northward to Bellingham, WA. Upon docking vessel, wash, and clean vessel. Accomplish required inspections and fender repairs. Remove existing and install new zinc anodes. Hull, freeboard and exterior decks require ultrasonic measurement of plating thickness and repair of areas below minimum thickness as needed. Accomplish blast and paint preservation of hull, freeboard, exterior decks and superstructure. Vessel requires inspection for damage and deterioration (hull, exterior decks, and tanks/voids plating and framing). Apply new non-skid system to exterior decks. Open, clean, ventilate, inspect, test, and maintain dry each tank/void. Accomplish partial preservation of QTY (24 EA) ballast tanks/voids. Accomplish access cover and watertight hatch and door repairs. Disinfect and certify potable water system. Pump and clean the interior surfaces of the CHT tank. Accomplish main deck repairs, hawse hole bulls eye and bolster repairs, and hull fendering system modifications. Accomplish the following modifications: hot water heater installation, awning replacement, A/C plant replacement and backup systems, switchboard upgrades, 1MC replacement and phone system upgrades, and CCTV upgrades. Undock the vessel. Verify vessel drawings and provide redline drawings to reflect actual conditions of the vessel. Conduct dock trials. Coordinate with the SUPERVISOR to support and accomplish all contract requirements prior to the availability end date. Arrange and coordinate the delivery of the vessel back to the Government with the Contracting Officer via the SUPERVISOR. Specific details of all work items and tasks required by the Statement of Work described in this Scope Overview are included in Section 3.0 of the Statement of Work. The vessel availability is scheduled to be 31 March 2027 through 31 March 2028. title: Notice of Opportunity (NOO) U.S. Army Reserve, 88th Readiness Division Energy Savings Performance Contract (ESPC)
description: U.S. Army Reserve, 88th RD has an objective to reduce energy consumption, reduce energy cost, and increase energy resiliency of multiple facilities located in Minnesota and Wisconsin. The 88th RD is seeking to identify additional Energy Conservation Measures (ECMs) that provide measurable energy and cost savings. Potential energy and water saving projects may include but are not limited to: envelope improvements, insulation upgrades, window upgrades, LED upgrades, geothermal heat pumps, lighting, controls, renewable energy generation including photovoltaic solar arrays, retro-commissioning, water conservation measures, heating, ventilation, air conditioning (HVAC) upgrades including boilers, furnaces, split systems, and chillers, battery energy storage systems (BESS), and Hydrogen Fuel Cells and microgrids. Additional ECMs of interest include re-tuning; retro-commissioning and re-commissioning; building automation and control systems; window replacement; minor building-envelope improvements; domestic hot-water system replacement; plug-load analysis and reduction, including refrigerators and freezers; water-leak detection; and other water-efficiency upgrades. The project will evaluate these and other cost-effective opportunities to modernize facilities, improve energy and water resilience, and support the 88th RD long-term energy, water conservation, and resiliency goals (as determined by 88th RD and ARIMD). These efforts align with statutory requirements under 10 U.S.C. � 2911 for energy security and resilience, and 42 U.S.C. � 8287 through the Department of Energy�s (DOE) Fourth-Generation Energy Savings Performance Contract (ESPC) Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) contract. description: 3M Versaflo TR-800-HIK Heavy Industry PAPR Kit Intrinsically Safe, Gray - 1 EachThe 3M Versaflo TR-800-HIK Heavy Industry PAPR Kit Intrinsically Safe is a complete powered air-purifying respirator (PAPR) system engineered for hazardous industrial environments, delivering intrinsically safe respiratory protection with a standard-capacity battery, intelligent airflow monitoring, and dependable all-day performance in demanding worksites. Featuring an intrinsically safe TR-800 powered air turbo, M-307 PAPR headgear, visual, audible, and vibrating low-flow and low-battery alarms, ergonomic belt-mounted design, and easy-to-use controls, this industrial PAPR respirator helps workers maintain a continuous supply of filtered breathing air, reduce respiratory fatigue, improve comfort during extended shifts, and support productivity in manufacturing, oil and gas, chemical processing, utilities, pharmaceutical production, confined space work, and other hazardous locations. The 3M Versaflo TR-800-HIK Heavy Industry PAPR Kit Intrinsically Safe is NIOSH approved and designed to help employers comply with OSHA respiratory protection requirements when used as part of a complete respiratory protection program

description: The contractor shall provide all labor, supervision, tools, equipment and transportation necessary to provide, install and maintain washers and dryers, on a rental basis, on Langley AFB, VA in accordance with (IAW) this performance work statement (PWS). The washers and dryers will be rented from the contractor, in new condition, and the contractor shall also perform quarterly inspections/preventative maintenance and perform repairs on an as needed basis. Questions in response to the solicitation are due NLT 1530 EST on 23 October 2026. The Government will provide a response to the received questions NLT close of business (COB) on 27 October 2026. The site visit for the subject solicitation will take place on Thursday, 22 October 2026 from 1000-1030 EST. If you plan to attend and/or require base access, please email SSgt Cameron Bettencourt, cameron.bettencourt@us.af.mil and copy Viviana Castillo Ramirez, viviana.castillo_ramirez@us.af.mil NLT 21 October 2026 at 1100 EST. Per Instructions to Offerors section, please ensure that both point of contacts are included in all communications/submissions.Quotes must be submitted via the PIEE Solicitation module.

description: SYNOPSIS: This is not a solicitation announcement. This is a sources sought synopsis only. This is NOT a request for proposals and in no way obligates the Government to award any contract. The purpose of this sources sought synopsis is to gain knowledge of commercially available products that may be of interest to the United States Coast Guard (USCG). The USCG Aviation Logistics Center is conducting market research to determine repair/overhaul sources described as follows: BACKGROUND: The U.S. Coast Guard (USCG) operates eighteen (18) HC-144 Maritime Patrol Aircraft, as well as fourteen (14) HC-27J aircraft. These Maritime Patrol Aircraft (MPA) are operated differently from general aviation in support of USCG search and rescue missions, as well as surveillance and reconnaissance missions. The USCG HC-144 and HC-27J missions require frequent operation at lower altitudes and in salt-laden environments. These environments accelerate corrosion on airframe structures, engines and components of the aircraft. The aircraft and its components are inspected by USCG personnel In Accordance With (IAW) the Original Equipment Manufacturer�s (OEM) periodic requirements and in conjunction with the USCG's specialized Asset Computerized Maintenance System (ACMS). The purpose of this sources sought synopsis is to gain knowledge of any commercially available repair and overhaul vendors that may be of interest to the United States Coast Guard (USCG). This notice is to assist the USCG in determining the potential sources capable of repair and overhaul services for the items listed below. The Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) is Moog Wolverhampton Limited. All components are required to be repaired and/or overhauled IAW OEM Specifications to include the latest OEM Revisions, Updates, and Service Bulletins. title: J048--Clinical Lab Bypass Loop System Install
description: Sources Sought Purpose The Department of Veterans Affairs, Network Contracting Office (NCO) 6 is seeking qualified contractors capable of installing a chilled-water bypass loop system serving the third-floor laboratory space. This Sources Sought notice is issued for market research and acquisition planning purposes only. It is not a solicitation, request for proposal, invitation for bid, or promise to award a contract. The VA is seeking responses from qualified small and other-than-small businesses, including firms capable of performing the work. Background The Central VA Healthcare System is requesting a new chiller to be installed on the roof of the third-floor laboratory. However, a chilled-water bypass loop system was not installed as part of the original work. Because the system lacks the required bypass loop, the chiller shuts down after operating for a period of time or upon reaching a predetermined operating condition. These shutdowns result in inadequate cooling and elevated temperatures within the laboratory space. The VA requires the installation of a bypass loop system and integration with the existing chiller, air-handling equipment, and Johnson Controls, Inc. (JCI) building automation/control system. Requested Information Interested firms are invited to submit a capability statement addressing the following: Company name, address, point of contact, telephone number, and email address. Unique Entity ID and CAGE code, if available. Business size and socioeconomic status, including any applicable: Small business status Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business status Veteran-Owned Small Business Status 8(a) status Woman-Owned Small Business status HUBZone status Confirmation of the firm s ability to perform the work as a prime contractor. Relevant experience installing chilled-water bypass loops, chiller piping systems, HVAC controls, or comparable systems. Experience integrating HVAC equipment with Johnson Controls or similar building automation systems. At least two relevant projects completed within the past five years, including: Customer name Contract or project value Location Dates of performance Description of work performed Point of contact and telephone number or email address Identification of proposed subcontractors and the work they would perform. Applicable licenses, certifications, bonding capacity, and safety qualifications. Any concerns, assumptions, or recommendations regarding the anticipated scope. Indication of whether the firm believes the requirement can be set aside for a particular small-business category. Contracting Specialist: Cedric Frasier Email: cedric.frasier@va.gov Response Due Date: November 2, 2026 @ 4PM ET. The subject line should read: Sources Sought Response Third-Floor Laboratory Chilled-Water Bypass Loop 36C24627Q0088 Important Notice This notice is for market research and acquisition planning only. The Government will not pay for information submitted in response to this notice, nor will it reimburse respondents for any costs associated with preparing or submitting a response. A response to this notice does not constitute an offer and will not be considered a proposal or quotation. The Government is not obligated to issue a solicitation, award a contract, or reimburse respondents for any costs. Respondents will not be notified individually of the results of the market research. Information submitted may be used to determine the appropriate acquisition strategy and solicitation requirements.

title: Cowboy Hat Stewardship IRSC - Lake Tahoe Basin Management Unit
description: This Sources Sought / Request for Information (RFI) is issued solely for market research and planning purposes. It does not constitute a solicitation or a promise to issue a solicitation in the future. The Government will not reimburse accompanying costs. Any answers or attachments provided are based upon the best information available at the time of the site visit and are subject to change. 1. Background & Purpose USDA Forest Service seeks capability statements from qualified vendors able to conduct forest thinning and vegetation treatments in areas burned by the Caldor Fire. The goals of the project are to reduce hazardous fuels and create conditions appropriate for reestablishing forested landscapes. Stewardship Authority shall be utilized to award an Integrated Resource Service Contract. In accordance with the approved NEPA decision, Cut-to-Length harvesting is the required logging mechanism. CTL typically consists of a harvester cutting and processing trees at the stump and a forwarder transporting the material to a designated landing location over a slash mat. The purpose of this SS/RFI is to gather information on vendor capabilities, invite prospective vendors to an organized site visit on 11/3/2026 before snow limits access, and provide draft documents to so that vendors can assess whether the opportunity is one to follow and potentially quote. 2. Anticipated Scope of Work The project objectives shall be met by performing the following service work. Cut, process, and forward to landings or pile included biomass in 3 units across 205 acres. Within these units, cut standing dead conifer trees and forward to landings or pile. Treat fuels by mechanically masticating existing dead and down material, project-generated slash and brush. Remove slash and large dead and down to landings when necessary to meet the fuels treatment specification. Remove biomass and cull logs from landings to off-Forest disposal sites. Construct temporary road to facilitate thinning treatment and decommission the roads prior to demobilization. Perform road maintenance and erosion control on roads used for biomass removal or otherwise damaged by Contractor�s operations. Perform hand thinning and piling if awarded. 3. Place of Performance The project is located on the Lake Tahoe Basin Management Unit in portions of Township 11N Range 18E Section 5, and Township 12N Range 18E Sections 32 and 33; Mount Diablo Meridian, approximately 0.5 miles southeast of the intersection of California Highway 89 and US Highway 50. 4. Period of Performance Anticipated start date: Early Summer 2027. Performance deadline: 9/15/2027. This deadline is linked to grant funding expiration. 5. Site Visit An organized site visit will occur on Tuesday, November 3, 2026, at 10:00 a.m. local time. Interested parties will meet in South Lake Tahoe, CA at the east end of Oneidas Street at the Forest Service Gate: 38�51'53.0"N 119�59'40.7"W. This location is south of Lake Tahoe Airport off of Pioneer Trail Road. Interested parties should email Karen Ruklic at karen.ruklic@usda.gov by 1:00 p.m. PT on November 2, 2026, if they plan to attend. 6. Requested Capability Statement Content Company information (UEI, address, email, POC, business size and socio-economic status). Relevant experience focused on thinning via Cut-to-Length logging system and hazardous fuel reduction. Key personnel and crew qualifications. Equipment lists and mobilization capabilities. Past performance references. 7. Response Instructions & Due Date Any information submitted by vendors to this this SS/RFI is voluntary. Responses should be submitted electronically to Karen Ruklic at karen.ruklic@usda.gov. All responses are due no later than Monday, November 2, 2026, at 1:00 p.m. PT.

This is a 100% total small business set-aside procurement issued under NAICS code 561210, Facilities Support Services by the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Vicksburg District (MVK). The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) Vicksburg District (MVK) has the continued responsibility for the operation and maintenance (O&M) of the Arkansas Lakes Flood Control Projects at DeGray Lake, Lake Ouachita, and Lake Greeson located in the state of Arkansas. title: J065--Notice of Intent to Sole Source Maintenance of Alaris Infusion Pumps
description: Statement of Work (SOW) Butler Healthcare Care Center (HCC) 1. BACKGROUND: The Butler Healthcare Care Center (hereafter referred to as Butler HCC or the Government ) has a requirement to add a new range of Internet Protocol (IP) addresses and a post-warranty, full maintenance agreement on the GuardRails software package and system utilized at the Butler HCC. 2. OBJECTIVE: The Government intends to award a single, Firm-Fixed Price contract for the services described in this Statement of Work (SOW). The period of performance under this contract is one year after receipt of order (ARO), with four additional one-year option periods, to be exercised at the Government s discretion. 3. PLACE OF PERFORMANCE: The tracking software is utilized at the main building of the Butler HHC Facility: Butler Healthcare Care Center (HCC) 353 North Duffy Road Butler, PA 16001 5. SCOPE OF WORK: Add a new range of IP addresses to existing Alaris System. Annual Maintenance and Support Services for the Alaris System software and components, billed in monthly installments, at the pricing levels stated for the Base and Option Years. Installation of the latest available software version if updated versions become available during the term of the agreement. Becton, Dickinson, and Company (BD) may install the newest version at the time-of-service delivery. Support of Guardrails Point-of-Care Software for PC Units and Modules, including applicable updates under BD s standard federal terms and conditions. Access to BD s Alaris Federal Terms and Conditions, incorporated by reference, governing software management, licensing, system requirements, and technical support. Compliance with Federal Information Processing Standards (FIPS) 140 2 operation requirements for the BD Alaris Packet Control Unit (PCU) wireless module (#4283), as applicable. All maintenance and support services identified in the vendor s Alaris Support Program (ASP) program as applicable. 6. PERFORMANCE DELIVERABLES: The Contractor shall provide performance deliverables in accordance with the Maintenance and Support Services described in the vendor quotation and BD s Alaris Federal Terms and Conditions. Deliverables include: Log into the designated server located at Veterans Administration (VA) Altoona, using existing and previously authorized access credentials, to perform a network configuration update. The required work consists of adding a new range of IP addresses to support devices that are already installed and previously connected to the VA network. No new equipment will be installed or connected as part of this effort, and no Personally Identifiable Information (PII) or sensitive data will be accessed, processed, or transmitted. This task is limited solely to updating network configuration parameters to reflect the new IP address assignments. Monthly invoicing for Maintenance and Support Fees, consistent with the annual amounts listed for Base and Option Years. Delivery and installation remote or on site as applicable of software updates, enhancements, or patches for Guardrails Suite MX software and Alaris Systems Manager, if newer versions become available during the contract period. Compliance with all BD warranty, licensing, and support terms, including user guide availability, acceptable use requirements, and software licensing restrictions. Notification to the Government of any required purchase order issuance prior to BD providing products or performing services under the Customer Order. Delivery of services only upon satisfaction of BD s order requirements: Customer execution of the Customer Order Issuance of a purchase order referencing the Customer Order CareFusion countersignature of the order These steps must occur before BD is obligated to ship products or perform services. Assurance that CareFusion personnel providing services comply with federal terms related to system use, data handling, intellectual property, compliance with laws, and product warranties. Support consistent with BD s federal customer schedules (e.g., Software Management Services for the Alaris System), as incorporated by reference in the vendor quote. 7. PERFORMANCE EXPECTATIONS: The Contractor shall provide comprehensive performance-driven support in alignment with the services outlined within the vendor s ASP. The following expectations incorporate the specific services and definitions provided in the vendor quotation and federal Alaris Software Management Services schedules: Quarterly Infusion Analytics Service data reports, including: executive summaries, detailed drug risk analyses, and retrospective infusion data accessible for up to two years. Remote analyst review shall be available via one quarterly call upon request. Installation and support of Guardrails Suite MX Software enhancements, including updates to PC Unit Software, Module Software, CQI Reporter, Guardrails Editor, and ASM. Includes remote installation of enhancements when applicable. Access to the Knowledge Portal for infusion technologies, including online portal access, training modules, and applicable user documentation. Monthly web-based refresher training for Guardrails Editor and CQI Reporter. Technical telephone support available Monday through Friday, 5 AM 5 PM PT, covering operation, configuration, and troubleshooting of the Alaris System and Alaris Systems Manager. Pharmacy Consultant and Clinical Infusion Data Consultant support for dataset review and interpretation. One annual on-site technical service visit (per 200 licensed units) for embedded software updates, CQI data downloads, and customized dataset uploads. One annual on-site RN Clinical Consultant visit (per 500 PC Units) to support practice reinforcement, compliance rounds, and infusion safety education. Hosted server system updates, including OS patching, ASM updates, and remote monitoring of the Alaris Systems Manager health and uptime. Tuition for up to two customer representatives to attend the Alaris System Data Workshop annually. 8. Point of Contact (POC): POC: TBA POC Phone Number: TBA POC Email: TBA

title: Request for Information: Additive Manufacturing
description: REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) � Additive Manufacturing THIS IS A REQUEST FOR INFORMATION ONLY. Naval Supply Systems Command (NAVSUP) � Weapon Systems Support (WSS) is conducting market research to identify potential sources with the capability to design, produce, and deliver end items using additive manufacturing (AM) methods for piece part components or entire assemblies. The Government is seeking information from qualified businesses on their ability to meet manufacturing, material, performance, testing, and quality assurance requirements applicable to these parts. In addition, this notice serves to gather industry perspectives on contracting structures (performance-based incentives under Firm-Fixed-Price contracts) and evaluation criteria for future competitive awards. Current candidate NIINs for additive manufacturing are listed in Attachment 1. This list is subject to change at any time at the Government's discretion and does not constitute a final determination for the use of additive manufacturing. Inclusion of an item on the attached list does not guarantee that the Government will issue requirements or solicitations for any item listed. The Government anticipates that Level I / SUBSAFE items may be eligible for additive manufacturing in the future. Government-Furnished drawings, Technical Data Packages (TDPs), and 3D CAD models will not be uploaded or provided with this notice. Interested vendors shall submit requested information in PDF format via email to hannah.m.forsyth.civ@us.navy.mil no later than the date and time indicated in this posting. Subject Line: �Request for Information: NAVSUP WSS Additive Manufacturing N0010427RZ058� Responses should include the following: Administrative Details: Company name, CAGE code, DUNS/UEI, and business size classification (large, small, 8(a), HUBZone, SDVOSB, WOSB, etc.). Manufacturing Capabilities & Subcontracting: Description of direct capabilities in additive manufacturing, or identification of intentions to utilize subcontractors/partners for additive manufacturing operations. Facilities, Equipment & Certifications: Information on relevant certifications (e.g., ISO 9001, AS9100, Level 1 / NAVSEA approvals), facilities, and equipment (e.g., type of AM modalities/machines, post-processing capabilities, heat treatment, and NDT/inspection methods). Past Performance: Examples of past performance related to similar AM parts or comparable military/commercial hardware, including contract numbers and descriptions. Interested Vendor: Indicate preference to be included on a mailing list for future additive manufacturing opportunities Performance-Based Incentives on FFP Contracts: NAVSUP WSS is seeking feedback and ideas regarding the structuring of performance-based incentives on Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) contracts for additive manufacturing Competitive Evaluation Criteria: NAVSUP WSS is seeking feedback and recommendations regarding effective, objective evaluation criteria for competitive awards The following draft documents are attached to this notice: Attachment 1: Candidate NIIN List Attachment 2: Additive Manufacturing Section H Special Contract Requirements � NON-LEVEL 1 Attachment 3: Additive Manufacturing Contract Data Requirements List (CDRL) NON-LEVEL 1 Respondents are also strongly encouraged to submit their AM capability within the NAVSUP Interested Vendor Database: https://mynavsup-public.nag.navy.mil/public/ops$public.business_vendor_form_new

description: Pre-Solicitation Notice Amendment for Navajo Area Abandoned Mines Response and Construction Services II (AMRCS II). This is a Request for Information (RFI) regarding the attached Draft Request for Proposal (DRFP). The DRFP is being released for COMMENT ONLY. This is not a synopsis proceeding the issuance of a solicitation. It is market research issued solely for information purposes - it does not constitute a Request for Proposal (RFP) or any other solicitation. This notice does not commit the U.S. Government to contract for any supply or service. The U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (US EPA) is not seeking proposals at this time. Responders are advised that the U.S. Government will not pay any cost incurred in response to this notice. All costs associated with responding to this notice will solely be at the interested parties' expense. Any information provided by industry to the Government as a result of this notice is voluntary. Not responding to this notice does not preclude participation in any future solicitation. It is recommended that interested parties monitor the FEDCONNECT website (https://www.fedconnect.net) for any information that may pertain to this notice. The information provided in this notice is subject to change and is not binding on the Government. The purpose of this RFI is to Request Comment on the DRFP for this requirement; which includes potential evaluation criteria for Navajo area- Abandoned Mines Response and Construction Services (AMRCS). To ensure the formal solicitation is executed in the most effective manner possible, we are posting the DRFP to offer an opportunity for industry to provide feedback. Your questions and input will be used to further refine, improve, or clarify these requirements. All Information and documentation posted under this notice are preliminary in nature and may be updated or amended prior to the release of the formal solicitation. NOTICE INFORMATION 1. SOLICITATION NUMBER: 68HE0926R0006 2. TITLE: Navajo Area- Abandoned Mines Response and Construction Services (AMRCS) 3. PRODUCT SERVICE CODE: F108- Hazardous Substance Removal, Cleanup, and Disposal Services 4. NAICS CODE: 562910- Environmental Remediation Services- Environmental Remediation Services a. Size Standard: 750 Employees 5. ANTICIPATED RFP RELEASE: Fall 2026 6. ANTICIPATED CONTRACT TYPE: Single award Indefinite Delivery/Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) 7. DESCRIPTION a. Background: Under the authority of Section 104 of the Comprehensive Environmental Response, Compensation, and Liability Act (CERCLA) or Super fund of 1980, as amended by the Superfund Amendments and Reauthorization Act (SARA); Subtitle I of the Resource Conservation and Recover y Act (RCRA) and pursuant to the National Oil and Hazardous Substances Pollution Contingency Plan (NCP) (40 CFR Part 300); and in accordance with any reauthorizations or amendment s to any of the above named statutes and new response legislation, the EPA has been delegated the responsibility to undertake response actions with respect to the release or threat of release of hazardous substances, or pollutants and contaminants, that pose an actual or potential threat to human health or welfare, or to the environment. b. Navajo Area Uranium Mines (USEPA Region 9) The Navajo Nation encompasses more than 27,000 square miles, spread amongst the Four Corners Region of the USA (Colorado, New Mexico, Utah, and Arizona). The unique geology of the region makes the Navajo Nation rich in uranium, a radioactive ore in high demand after the development of atomic power and weapons at the close of World War II in the 1940s. Approximately four million tons of uranium ore were extracted during mining operations within the Navajo Nation from 1944 to 1986. Many Navajo people worked the mines, often living and raising families in close proximity to the mines and mills. Uranium mining and milling activities no longer occur on Navajo lands, but the legacy of these activities remains, including more than 500 abandoned uranium mine claims with thousands of mine features such as pits, trenches, holes, etc., and homes and drinking water sources with elevated levels of uranium, radium and other radionuclides. Uranium and other elements (selenium, arsenic, etc.) associated with mine and mill sites also occur naturally at elevated levels in rock, soil, surface water, and groundwater across the Navajo Nation and the broader Four Corners region. USEPA maintains a strong partnership with the Navajo Nation and, since 1994, the USEPA Superfund Program has provided technical assistance and funding to assess potentially contaminated sites and develop a response. In August 2007, the USEPA Superfund Program compiled a Comprehensive Database and Atlas of all known uranium mines on the Navajo Nation. In October 2007, at the request of the U.S. House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform, EPA, along with the Bureau of Indian Affairs (BIA), the Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC), the Department of Energy (DOE), and the Indian Health Service (IHS) developed a coordinated https://www.epa.gov/navajo-nation-uranium-cleanup to address uranium contamination in consultation with Navajo Nation EPA. d. Region 9 The primary hazardous substance on all the sites referenced in the requirement�s Statement of Work (SOW) is radiological mine and mine related waste; therefore, a significant knowledge base of radiological material handling, environmental data interpretation, and data collection will be required to perform the activities within this SOW. The terrain to access site locations is rough, water is scarce, and the weather is often extreme in most areas. The trails and/or roads to the sites are not improved or maintained. To reach the site locations, 4-wheel drive vehicles (capable of drives over rough dirt/rocky roads) and/or hiking long distances is required. Roads can become impassable in wet weather, and conditions can change quickly. In summer, the conditions are hot and dry; in winter, elevations make them subject to severe cold and high winds. Due to the quick changes in the weather, be aware of the danger of flash floods. While this danger is greatest during the summer monsoon season (July through September), flash floods can occur at any time of the year. e. Purpose and Objectives: The purpose of the Navajo Area Abandoned Mines Response and Construction Services (AMRCS) contract is to provide cleanup, response, and construction services to the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA), primarily at former uranium mining-related sites on or within the Navajo Nation (within EPA Region 9 in Arizona and New Mexico). 7. DESCRIPTION OF INFORMATION REQUESTED: The USEPA is seeking comments on the attached DRFP. The Government will consider all comments, questions, and issues raised by all prospective offerors in formulating requirements for any resultant solicitation document. The information contained here reflects the Government's anticipated requirements as of the date on this posting. The purpose of this notice is to solicit comments regarding a possible acquisition. The issuance of this notice is designed to gather as much information as possible to ensure that the Government's requirements are clear and concise; and possibly improve the requirements based on industry best practices and lessons learned, which may be stated in a future solicitation. SUBMITTAL INFORMATION A cover page and an executive summary may be included in the response, but is not required. All interested parties may respond. At a minimum, responses should include the following: a. Business name, SAM Unique Entity ID, business address, size and type of business (e.g., Large Business, Small Business, 8(a), HubZone, Woman Owned Small Business etc.) pursuant to the applicable NAICS code, and the name, telephone number, mailing address, and email address of a point of contact having authority and knowledge to discuss responses with Government representatives.
